name: mia-rosie-midnight-mysteries
description: Mia & Rosie: Midnight Mysteries — English, family-friendly animated bedtime-magic Shorts for ages 6-10: Mia and her living doll Rosie talk on camera, 60 s episodes of six 10 s scenes.
voice: No narrator. Mia is a bright, curious child; Rosie is a magical doll with a tiny, soft, friendly voice. Short, warm, spoken lines.
style_rules: Fiction for children aged 6 to 10 and family viewing: friendship, curiosity, kindness and gentle magic; nothing scary.
Each episode is six 10-second scenes of dialogue between Mia and Rosie, with one visible change per scene (a glow, a discovery, a reveal) and a last image that closes the episode.
The dialogue comes from the owner's episode script and is used word for word; scenes keep their order, their location and their dialogue.
Every line is short enough to be spoken in the scene's seconds (about 0.42 s per word) with room for pauses and sound.
Continuity (from Episode 1 revisions): show every landmark the episode uses (toy shelf, toy chest, window, bed) in scene 1, so no prop appears for the first time mid-episode.

A prop or effect changes state once only (a chest opens once, a star appears once); each recurring object keeps one look across all six scenes, and one scene's last state is the next scene's first state.
visual_rules: Expressive cinematic 3D animation, midnight blue and lavender with crimson and soft golden accents; warm moonlit bedroom magic.

Recurring characters, the bedroom, the toy chest and the golden star get locked descriptors in Look anchors, pasted verbatim into every visual prompt where they appear, so faces, clothes and set never drift.
Mia and Rosie talk on camera, so mouths move only for the character speaking the quoted line.
No text, subtitles, readable words, watermark or logos.
idea_wells: Haunted toys, music boxes and dolls with a clue instead of a jump scare
Bedroom mysteries: footsteps, shadows, mirrors, closets
Original folklore-style enchanted forests and magical objects
